Chart shows fuel subsidies reduced inflation by estimated 2 percentage points. Chart showing counterfactual fuel prices with/without subsidies. Covid-19 differentiated sectoral impact chart. Banxico response to inflationary pressures: acceleration in pace of monetary tightening from 25bp initial hikes to 50bp and 75bp hikes as inflation broadened. Policy rate at 9.25%, about 6pp above U.S. Fed. Markets pricing terminal rate ~10.5% by Q1 2023. Directly addresses 5B.3 (monetary policy conduct) and 5B.9 (policy response to inflation shock).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0011", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3"], "relevance_strength": "weak", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0010", "unit-0012"], "explanation": "Financial conditions have tightened: IMF Financial Conditions Index shows moderate increase by June 2022 but below past peaks. Interest rates on peso-denominated securities at highest since Global Financial Crisis. Yield on 1-year government bond rose 250+ bps. Real yield on inflation-linked Udibonos up 80bps. Foreign-currency yields also rose. Chart of market-implied inflation breakevens across countries. Portfolio flows: moderate outflows continued, peso broadly stable, supported by rising interest rate differential, fiscal discipline, monetary policy commitment to price stability, solid remittances. International reserves adequate at 125% ARA metric coverage. Relevant to 5B.3 (financial conditions and monetary transmission).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0012", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0011", "unit-0013"], "explanation": "Credit growth recovering despite tighter conditions. Large institutions maintain ample liquidity buffers. As global oil prices rose, authorities smoothed retail fuel prices and stabilized prices of essential food items. Fiscal cost of fuel pricing regime rose following Russian invasion of Ukraine, resulting in higher-than-budgeted subsidies in 2022H1. PEMEX benefited from higher oil prices; EBITDA doubled to USD 23bn in H1 2022. Relevant to 5B.3 (banking system resilience) and 5B.9 (fuel subsidy response to shock).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0013", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9", "5B.10"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0012", "unit-0014"], "explanation": "OUTLOOK AND RISKS: Growth projected 2.1% in 2022 and 1.2% in 2023. Weaker domestic and U.S. demand expected to slow activity and employment. Current account to widen to ~1% GDP. Box 1 (2023 Budget Proposal): targets small deficit increase (3.8% to 4.1% GDP) due to interest payments. Fiscal stance neutral in 2023 per staff. Expenditure increase accommodates higher interest payments, social programs (non-contributory pensions), priority infrastructure. No tax code changes; continued anti-evasion efforts. Relevant to 5B.3 (fiscal stance), 5B.9 (shock outlook), 5B.10 (trajectory projection).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0014", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0013", "unit-0015"], "explanation": "Inflation projected to plateau ~8.5% in H2 2022 then decline gradually to midpoint of target band mid-2024, assuming policy rate raised to ~10% by early 2023. Balance of risks tilted to upside for inflation. Downside risks to growth: higher global inflation, sharper tightening of global financial conditions, sharper U.S. slowdown, additional supply shocks from Ukraine war, domestic inflation persistence, new COVID variants, climate risks. Upside: nearshoring dynamics, smaller-than-expected U.S. spillovers. Directly addresses 5B.3 (inflation trajectory) and 5B.9 (shock risk assessment).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0015", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "weak", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0014", "unit-0016"], "explanation": "Continued risks discussion: medium-term risks include pandemic scarring or policy uncertainty lowering potential output, climate-change induced risks. See inflation falling in 2023 from normalization of supply shocks, fiscal measures for fuel prices, decisive monetary policy. U.S. slowdown headline risk. Nearshoring could benefit Mexico. Faster-than-expected global tightening could spark capital outflow pressures. Relevant to 5B.9 (shock risk assessment and response).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0016", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0015", "unit-0017"], "explanation": "Box 2: Global Tightening and Inflation Scenario - G20MOD model simulation of three-layer downside shock: (1) temporary oil/food price shock (+10%/+50%), raising headline inflation ~1% above baseline; (2) second layer with inflation expectations dislocation causing sharper domestic policy rate increases, output falling >1% below baseline by H1 2023; (3) third layer with 1% domestic demand decline, bringing output >2% below baseline. Since June 2021, gradually larger rate increases brought ex ante real policy rate to moderately restrictive level (~4%) by September 2022. Appropriately calibrated response to upward inflation surprises and sequential delays in returning to target. Policy rate of at least 10% required for inflation to return to 3% target within ~2 years. Charts show inflation and expectations data and real ex-ante policy rates vs. peers. Charts showing inflation expectations and processed food prices. Philips curve estimates confirm backward-looking elements in Mexico's inflation process. Risk management approach argues for policy rates to rise further and stay firmly restrictive. Ex ante real rate peaking >5% in 2023. Addresses 5B.3 (monetary credibility) and 5B.9 (shock risk assessment).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0019", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0018", "unit-0020"], "explanation": "Clear monetary policy communication recommended to increase effectiveness during significant inflation uncertainty. Directly addresses 5B.3 (policy communication/transparency).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0020", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0019", "unit-0021"], "explanation": "FISCAL MEASURES: Authorities used largely untargeted subsidies to mitigate cost of living rises totaling ~2% GDP. (2) Food price mitigation through preexisting programs (fertilizers for small farmers, subsistence farming support) at smaller budgetary cost. Higher food and energy prices increased deficit by only ~0.25% GDP as subsidies offset by higher oil revenues. Admin increased universal social pensions; projected minimum wage rise from 42% to 59% of median formal sector wage between 2018-2022. Real per capita labor income increased ~5% y/y by mid-2022. Priority is restoring low stable inflation. Restrictive monetary + neutral fiscal = appropriate policy mix. However, continuing large minimum wage increases will likely add to inflation pressures, counter-purpose to monetary/fiscal policies and potentially reducing formal employment for lower income workers. Authorities emphasized anti-inflationary fiscal measures helped mitigate effects on most exposed. Fuel price stabilization central to supporting households and restraining inflation per President's commitment. Note pricing mechanism has dampening second-round inflation effects. Food measures leveraged existing policies. Goal to support historically underserved agricultural communities with expected positive effects on yields. Charts showing exchange rates against USD and inflation/policy rate gaps. MANAGING POTENTIAL DOWNSIDE RISKS - FISCAL POLICY: Fiscal policy could better prepare for downside risks. Neutral stance appropriate for modest slowdown; more targeted support for poorer households should downside risks materialize. Mexico's fiscal framework (balanced budget rule, debt issuance constraints) limits countercyclical policy scope. Recommendations: (1) change retail fuel price regime to create room for targeted support during prolonged oil price increases; (2) implement proposed reforms to fiscal framework to enhance flexibility. Addresses 5B.3 (fiscal framework constraints) and 5B.9 (downside risk preparation).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0024", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.9"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0023", "unit-0025"], "explanation": "FEIP stabilization fund reserves fell to <0.1% GDP (extensive pandemic usage; restrictive replenishment mechanism). Minimum 0.3% GDP needed for sufficient fiscal policy response. Recent amendments to FRBL proposed to bring FEIP reserves closer to desired level using headroom against debt ceiling. Longer-term comprehensive reforms needed: well-calibrated debt anchor, broader expenditure coverage in structural spending rule, medium-term fiscal strategy with post-shock adjustment path, tighter escape clause triggers, strengthened fiscal council role. FCL provides additional external buffer. Charts showing exchange rates vs USD and inflation/policy rate gaps. Capital adequacy ratios high and rising; liquidity ratios comfortable. Banking system demonstrated strong resilience in solvency/liquidity stress tests under 2022 FSAP. Systemic vulnerabilities and liquidity risks broadly contained given high capital buffers, low private sector leverage, no stretched asset prices. Monitoring needed on bank loans and non-financial corporate health given rapid rate rises. Charts showing NFC average loan rates and total bank lending. Addresses 5B.3 (financial system resilience) and 5B.10 (institutional durability).", "exclusion_reason": null}, {"schema_version": "chunk_routing_decision_v1", "source_id": "MAC-010", "source_sha256": "8fac4146590dbe2ed458f7356748f5880d021e03cc4982b1e7efe083d33f622a", "chunk_id": "unit-0029", "included": true, "relevant_question_ids": ["5B.3", "5B.5"], "relevance_strength": "material", "adjacent_chunk_ids": ["unit-0028", "unit-0030"], "explanation": "Authorities should enhance financial system resilience: (1) Strengthen autonomy and resources of regulatory agencies and legal protection of supervisors. (2) CNBV should improve supervisory techniques, simplify risk-based rating system, enable consolidated supervision of all financial conglomerates. (3) System-wide liquidity risks contained but bear continued monitoring; Banxico Emergency Liquidity Assistance framework could be enhanced. (4) CNBV should closely monitor loan concentration risks and Pillar 2 requirements. Strengthen bank resolution and recovery. (5) Enhance cybersecurity approach. (6) Climate risks manageable but tail risks will worsen without resilience investments.
